Yes, you can have multiple United credit cards at one time. Unlike some other airline credit cards, United's cards don't have a broad restriction that prevents you from holding multiple cobranded cards.

You could hold a for its TravelBank Cash and 10,000-mile award discount, the for lounge access and a for business expenses.

There's also an incentive to pair a personal and business United card: Both United business cards offer 5,000 bonus miles each account anniversary if you're also the primary cardmember on a personal United card.

Holding multiple United cards won't make sense for infrequent flyers, since benefits like free checked bags and priority boarding overlap on multiple cards. However, for loyal customers, the collection of slightly different perks and cardholder PQP bonuses could justify the cost of paying multiple annual fees.

Yes, you can get the same United credit card more than once. However, you will only earn another welcome offer if you no longer hold that card and at least 24 months have passed since you received the new-cardmember bonus.

Remember, Chase counts from the date you receive the bonus, not from when you open or close the account.

If you are an authorized user on someone else's United card, Chase does not consider that being a current cardholder for the purposes of that card's bonus restrictions. In other words, you can still apply for your own version of that card and earn its welcome bonus.

However, an authorized-user account may appear on your credit report and increase your 5/24 count.

If you're denied because of an authorized-user account, you may be able to explain the situation to Chase by calling the reconsideration line, although approval isn't guaranteed.

If you're interested in both a personal and business United card, applying for the business card first often makes sense. That's because the business card won't add to your 5/24 limit and tip you over the edge.

However, if you're applying for multiple personal United cards, the order you apply shouldn't matter. Pick whichever card is your highest priority first, considering its benefits and how its current offer compares with past bonuses.

The best choice depends on how often you fly United and which benefits you'll actually use.

The is often a good starting point, since it offers strong benefits like a free checked bag and single-use lounge passes, and it has no annual fee in the first year. The offers TravelBank Cash and an annual award discount for more serious United loyalists, and the is best suited to frequent flyers who value ongoing lounge access.

United's eligibility rules are friendly to new applicants.

For the Gateway, Explorer, Quest, United Business and United Club Business cards, you're in a strong position if you don't currently hold the exact card and haven't received its welcome bonus within the past 24 months, while the United Club card has a minor caveat that won't impact most applicants.

#6091. Beijing's hidden chokehold could derail Trump's $50B plan to fix America's aging skies

As the Trump administration seeks $50 billion from Congress to replace aging air traffic control equipment after Friday’s nationwide ground stop, China’s control of the rare earth supply chain could complicate the overhaul.

Can the United States modernize its critical infrastructure without relying on China?

Amid the fallout from Friday’s nationwide ground stop that halted air travel and upended plans for millions of passengers, the Trump administration blamed aging air traffic control infrastructure, pointing fingers at past administrations and calling on lawmakers to approve billions in new modernization funding.

"Essentially, what you saw on Friday was very, very old equipment that had a heart attack," President Donald Trump told reporters Monday at the White House before departing for Asia.

DUFFY VOWS TO MODERNIZE AGING AIR TRAFFIC SYSTEM AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

Aviation specialists work inside the FAA's SMART Center, where technology combines weather, flight path and air traffic data to help identify potential congestion and improve flight efficiency. (Courtesy Department of Transportation)

The problem, one expert told Fox News Digital, is that China holds a near-monopoly over the global rare earth supply chain. While rare earth elements are relatively abundant in nature, Beijing dominates the processing stages required to turn raw ore into usable industrial components.

"For the FAA, radars, satellite systems, complex electrical systems, precision motors, navigation systems — all of these require rare earths inside them," said Anupam Ghildyal, chief growth officer for REalloys, a North American critical minerals and rare earth company.

AMERICA DEPENDS TOO MUCH ON CHINA FOR ESSENTIAL MINERALS. WE NEED TO DIG OUR FUTURE

Rare earth magnets are displayed in the showroom at Inner Mongolia Baotou Steel Rare-Earth Hi-Tech Co. in Baotou, Inner Mongolia, China. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"For the FAA to upgrade the infrastructure, you need all of these components, and those components have to be manufactured here because China can limit the supply of these components to the U.S.," he added. "But to manufacture these components in the U.S., we need the basic raw materials to make them from, which is something we do not have."

Beijing's stranglehold on rare earth minerals could bottleneck U.S. efforts before they get off the ground, Ghildyal warned, noting that China has the ability to slow-walk or block much-needed materials.

THE WEST STILL DOESN’T GRASP THE DANGER OF CHINA’S RARE EARTH ENDGAME

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy discusses the Federal Aviation Administration's SMART technology, which uses flight and weather data to help air traffic controllers identify congestion and recommend more efficient routes. (Courtesy Department of Transportation)

"100% they can, and they've been doing it," he said.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has requested $50 billion in additional funding from Congress to overhaul and modernize the nation's air traffic control system, while the White House is urging lawmakers to fund the replacement of decades-old copper wiring and aging control towers.

VETERAN PILOT: CONGRESS MUST ACT TO UPDATE 'ARCHAIC' FAA TECH THAT IS 'PUTTING AMERICANS IN DANGER'

A logo of rare earth magnets manufacturer JL Mag appears on a building in Baotou, Inner Mongolia, China, on April 6, 2026. (REUTERS)

"So you saw a telecom issue on Friday. We’re replacing old copper wires with fiber, but this is an old architecture of a network," Duffy said during an appearance on Fox News' "Hannity." "You’ve seen Newark go down. You’ve seen Dallas go down. You saw all of New York go down just a couple of months ago because of telecom issues. I want to build a brand-new architecture of a resilient telecom network that’s worthy of 2026 and worthy of America."

China didn't always dominate the rare earth minerals trade. Many companies began outsourcing those functions overseas, which China gladly took over.

GOV MIKE DUNLEAVY: CHINA IS HOLDING CRITICAL MINERALS HOSTAGE. ALASKA CAN HELP END THE THREAT

Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are slated to meet this week while Trump is in China for a series of high-level regional summits where trade is expected to be among the main issues discussed. China has cornered the market on rare earth mineral processing, which could complicate U.S. efforts to modernize its air traffic infrastructure, one expert said. (REUTERS)

"The problem is we are starting from pretty much close to zero," said Ghildyal. "Back in the 1980s and 1990s, we actually processed a lot of rare earths, made a lot of magnets, and then we decided that these processes are too laborious and too toxic, so let's offshore them. So we taught the Chinese how to do it, and over the last 40 years they've been doing it."

Rebuilding the nation’s airspace hardware relies heavily on specialized magnets and minerals dominated by China, Ghildyal said — an issue looming large ahead of Trump’s Thursday summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

TRUMP BRINGS TWO DIVIDED CABINET HEAVYWEIGHTS TO CHINA AS CONTROVERSY HANGS OVER HIGH-STAKES TALKS

"China uses it as leverage on the negotiating table," Ghildyal said. "I would assume they want AI chips. We want their rare earth materials, and that's how these transactions happen."

He noted that U.S. demand for neodymium magnets sits around 50,000 tons annually, far outpacing domestic production.

"We'll make about 500 tons this year, so we are making 1% of what we need," Ghildyal said. "So that 99% gap is not going away tomorrow or in the next two or three years. It's a five-to-10-year journey, but I think we should all be ashamed of ourselves if 10 years down the line, we are not independent of China for these critical materials."

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

#6090. How Marriott Members Can Sometimes Earn Points Twice On The Same Spending

A Marriott Bonvoy member reports earning qualifying spend or extra points by charging gift card purchases to the room bill even though Marriott expressly excludes gift card purchases from the spending requirement for Ambassador status. Ambassador takes 100 qualifying nights and $23,000 in annual qualifying spend. Someone staying at inexpensive and even moderately-priced hotels can clear the nights while falling well short on dollars. If a gift card counts when you buy it, you could move future hotel spending into the current qualification year. And if the purchase and the eventual hotel stay both earn points, you’ve earned twice on the same money. An April 4 report on US Card Forum laid out some properties where this worked, and where it didn’t. Property   Reported result Ritz-Carlton Waikiki spa   Gift cards charged to the room counted toward qualifying spend. St. Regis Longboat Key   Two $1,500 cards purchased, then used at checkout; the member reports an extra round of points. Tampa EDITION   Allowed the gift-card room charge; no separate points or spending total supplied. JW Marriott Clearwater   Refused to put the purchase on the room bill. Unnamed hotel, separate commenter   A charge labeled “gc” reached the folio but earned no points. Marriott’s terms (section 4.2.b.v) exclude Marriott Gift Card purchases from Annual Qualifying Spend. The Ambassador help page says the same thing. This comes down to how the hotel records the charge and sends it to Marriott. If a gift card sale goes through as an eligible incidental, the loyalty system credits the amount without recognizing what was actually sold. A properly identified gift card entry gets excluded. There are two places this can fail: the hotel can refuse the room charge, or accept it but keep it out of the amount eligible for points and status. An employee saying “yes, we can charge that to your room” doesn’t tell you whether it will post as eligible spend. I’ve covered another example of hotel level accounting producing more Ambassador credit than you’d expect. In 2024, the Renaissance Dallas advertised a rate with 30% additional qualifying spend for $20 extra per night. That suggested how the property’s handling of a charge can affect the way Marriott credits it. If you’re a Marriott person, who’s going to spend money with them anyway (clearly an Ambassador member does) this is an interesting thing to experiment with but I also wouldn’t hit it too hard with an Ambassador account that I valued. Me, I haven’t been an Ambassador since the end of the Starwood days. Marriott’s terms (section 4.2.b.v) exclude Marriott Gift Card purchases from Annual Qualifying Spend. The Ambassador help page says the same thing.

This comes down to how the hotel records the charge and sends it to Marriott. If a gift card sale goes through as an eligible incidental, the loyalty system credits the amount without recognizing what was actually sold. A properly identified gift card entry gets excluded.

There are two places this can fail: the hotel can refuse the room charge, or accept it but keep it out of the amount eligible for points and status. An employee saying “yes, we can charge that to your room” doesn’t tell you whether it will post as eligible spend.

I’ve covered another example of hotel level accounting producing more Ambassador credit than you’d expect. In 2024, the Renaissance Dallas advertised a rate with 30% additional qualifying spend for $20 extra per night. That suggested how the property’s handling of a charge can affect the way Marriott credits it.

If you’re a Marriott person, who’s going to spend money with them anyway (clearly an Ambassador member does) this is an interesting thing to experiment with but I also wouldn’t hit it too hard with an Ambassador account that I valued. Me, I haven’t been an Ambassador since the end of the Starwood days.

It still requires staying at a Marriott property. There aren’t enough points available to make that worth it.

#6088. Hyatt And Delta Launch Extra Points On Flights And Hotel Stays—But Standard Coach Tickets Don’t Qualify

Hyatt and Delta have launched extra points on flights and hotel stays, with airline status, lounge passes and hotel free night awards coming next year. But there’s a big restriction: even a Hyatt Globalist buying a regular Delta coach ticket earns no Hyatt points. That’s not ‘basic economy doesn’t count’ – it’s listerally standard main cabin coach that earns nothing. The companies announced their partnership in September. Now we know how the benefits actually work. This brings back some of what Hyatt members lost when American Airlines stopped reciprocal points earning at the end of 2024. But Delta excludes regular coach, gives Hyatt’s lowest elite tier half as many points, and pays hotel guests in a less valuable airline currency (SkyMiles). Who Earns Extra Points And Miles Start by linking your World of Hyatt and Delta SkyMiles accounts. Ongoing extra earning depends on your status: Your Status   Additional Earnings Delta Silver, Gold, Platinum or Diamond Medallion   1 SkyMile per eligible dollar spent with Hyatt, on top of Hyatt points Hyatt Discoverist   1 Hyatt point per $2 of eligible Delta premium cabin spending, on top of SkyMiles Hyatt Explorist, Globalist or Lifetime Globalist   1 Hyatt point per eligible dollar of Delta premium cabin spending, on top of SkyMiles Hyatt status qualifies you for Hyatt points on eligible Delta flights. Delta status qualifies you for SkyMiles on eligible Hyatt spending. For flights, Delta Comfort, Premium Select, First Class and Delta One qualify. Basic, Classic and Extra fare versions qualify when they’re sold in one of those cabins. So basic extra legroom coach qualifies, full fair regular coach doesn’t. . The flight earning rules also require: A Delta marketed and operated flight, with a Delta-issued ticket beginning 006. Your SkyMiles number attached before departure and Hyatt elite status when the flight is completed. A qualifying paid ticket. Eligible spending includes the base fare and airline imposed surcharges, but excludes government taxes, airport fees and amounts paid with miles. These are Hyatt bonus points. They don’t count as base points toward Hyatt status or lifetime Globalist. For hotel spending, eligible room charges, incidentals and qualifying purchases without an overnight stay can earn SkyMiles. Mr & Mrs Smith and The Venetian qualify when booked through Hyatt. Homes & Hideaways and FIND experiences are excluded. Hyatt Nights Can Earn Delta Credits, Lounge Visits And Status Beginning January 1, 2027, linked Hyatt members will have Delta options among their Milestone Rewards. These are choices, so you’ll need to compare them with the other rewards available at the same threshold. The specific awards are: Hyatt Qualification   Delta Reward Choice 20 qualifying nights or 35,000 base points   $25 Delta eCertificate 40 qualifying nights or 65,000 base points   $75 Delta eCertificate 60 qualifying nights or 100,000 base points   $100 Delta eCertificate 70, 80 or 90 qualifying nights   Two single visit Delta Sky Club passes 100 qualifying nights   Delta Gold Medallion status 150 qualifying nights   Delta Platinum Medallion status, without Choice Benefits The flight certificates and lounge passes expire one year after issuance. Each lounge pass covers one person for one visit with a qualifying same-day boarding pass (basic economy passengers excluded). The status awards are for your own account. They don’t provide anything extra if you already hold that tier or higher, and selecting the same status again doesn’t extend it. Platinum at 150 nights is potentially attractive, albeith without the Choice Benefits that normally come with that status (e.g. four Regional Upgrade Certificates). Delta Elites Can Choose Hyatt Free Nights Starting February 1, 2027, for the 2028 Medallion Year, Delta is adding: A Hyatt Category 1–4 free night as a Platinum Choice Benefit. A Hyatt Category 1–7 free night as a Diamond Choice Benefit. These aren’t extra certificates automatically handed to every Platinum and Diamond. You select one instead of another Choice Benefit. No new option to redeem SkyMiles directly for Hyatt free night certificates was announced, like we’d seen with the American partnership. Perhaps the biggest loss is Hyatt redemptions for American Airlines status for a day. Launch Bonuses Don’t Require Elite Status All linked members can participate in the launch offers: November 17–December 31, 2026: Register separately and complete a qualifying Hyatt stay to earn one additional qualifying night credit. That’s one bonus night total, not double nights for the entire stay. January 4–February 15, 2027: Complete your first eligible paid Delta Comfort-or-higher flight to earn 1,000 bonus Hyatt points. January 4–February 15, 2027: Complete your first qualifying Hyatt stay to earn 1,000 bonus SkyMiles. Paid and award stays qualify for the hotel promotions. Mr & Mrs Smith and The Venetian bookings through Hyatt qualify, while Homes & Hideaways doesn’t. The year-end stay must finish after registration and by December 31. For the January hotel offer, checkout must be by February 15. There’s also an Alila Mayakoba trip sweepstakes through November 23. Hyatt says reciprocal status challenges are coming. Is This Better Than Hyatt’s American Airlines Partnership? There are two different American partnerships to compare against. The original version, which ran through 2024, was better for everyday earning. Hyatt Discoverists earned the same one point per dollar on American airfare as Globalists, and regular coach counted. American elites earned a mile per eligible Hyatt dollar, and those miles also counted as Loyalty Points once that status system was introduced. Delta’s hotel earning has the same nominal mileage rate, but American miles are worth more. And there’s no status credit from those points. American’s final double earning terms also covered eligible FIND and Homes & Hideaways spending, both excluded here. On the flight side you’re earning Hyatt points either way, so the problem isn’t SkyMiles valuation. It’s the cabins that don’t qualify and the halved Discoverist rate. The 2025 American redesign removed double dipping and largely made members pay for partner benefits with their own points or by giving up another reward. Delta restores some actual additional earnings. The milestone comparison is mixed: Flight credits can be more useful than seat coupons. American offered two Preferred Seat coupons at 20 and 30 nights, then two Main Cabin Extra coupons at 40 and 50. Delta status starts later. American Gold was a choice at 70, 80 and 90 Hyatt nights. Delta offers lounge passes there, with its first announced status award at 100 nights. At 150 nights, Delta offers a higher tier. American’s offer topped out at Platinum. Delta Platinum is its third tier, although withholding Choice Benefits takes away a valuable part of the package. American also gave ConciergeKey members Hyatt Globalist and offered Hyatt status choices to other AAdvantage members. We’ll see what reciprocal status offers look like. It’s worth linking accounts and registering for the extra Hyatt night if there’s a stay coming up. #6087. Chase Adds Qantas And Cathay Pacific Transfers—More Access To Premium Award Seats

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

Chase is adding Qantas and Cathay Pacific as 1:1 transfer partners on November 18. For me, the biggest value is access to business and first class award seats that these airlines don’t make available to members of other frequent flyer programs.

These are Chase’s first new airline transfer partners in more than five years. And they’re an unambiguously positive addition, even if neither becomes the program most cardmembers use most often.

Eligible cards include Chase Sapphire Reserve, Sapphire Preferred, Sapphire Reserve for Business, Ink Business Preferred and J.P. Morgan Reserve. Both new partners transfer at 1:1. Hyatt transfers are now less generous for Sapphire Preferred and Ink Business Preferred: 4 Chase points become 3 Hyatt points, while the Reserve cards retain 1:1. That distinction doesn’t apply to these new airline partners. Chase Sapphire Reserve® (See rates and fees) is a strong card for actual spending, with 4 points per dollar on flights and hotels booked directly and 3 points per dollar on dining. Adding more transfer partners makes the value of those points even greater. Why I Want Qantas Points Chase already had ways to book oneworld flights through programs like British Airways and Iberia. But being able to book an airline doesn’t mean having access to all of its award seats. Airlines increasingly keep more of their premium cabin availability for their own members. As I explained when Rove added Qantas transfers, Qantas offers its members award space that American AAdvantage, Alaska and British Airways members can’t book. I have family in Australia and have had real success finding Qantas business class awards when there’s flexibility over the U.S. gateway and travel date. I’ll set alerts across several flights rather than insist on one. Some flight between Australia and the U.S. will inevitably open up with a couple of business class awards, usually around 60 days out. Qantas can also be useful for Emirates redemptions. I’d generally rather book the same available Emirates business class seat through Copa ConnectMiles, though. Copa charges 80,000 miles one way between the U.S. and Dubai in business class without fuel surcharges. And Qantas is no longer an unrestricted way around Emirates’ first class award limits. Booking Emirates first class with Qantas points requires Qantas Silver status or higher, and passengers must be at least nine years old. Cathay Offers More Award Space And Lower British Airways Surcharges Cathay Pacific is similar. Its own members get access to far more premium cabin award space than members of partner programs. Asia Miles prices can be high, though. I also like Asia Miles for reducing fuel surcharges on British Airways awards, particularly compared with booking through American AAdvantage. It’s also notable that Chase’s Cathay transfer rate is better than American Express’s. American Express transfers 1,000 Membership Rewards points to just 800 Asia Miles. An award requiring 100,000 Asia Miles takes 100,000 Chase points versus 125,000 Amex points (without transfer bonus). American Express, Citi, Capital One and Rove already partner with both Qantas and Cathay. Chase is catching up with these. I wouldn’t transfer points just because these options have been added. Chase Is Finally Adding Airline Partners Again Chase’s last new transfer partner was Wyndham Rewards in February 2026. Its last new airline partner was Air Canada Aeroplan on August 3, 2021. I welcomed Wyndham because it showed Chase was building out Ultimate Rewards, even though I had little interest in transferring points there. Qantas and Cathay are programs I can see myself using. They bring Chase to 12 airline transfer programs and four hotel programs. I also wonder whether these relationships could lead to more Points Boost opportunities. With Points Boost, Chase can use discounts it negotiates on paid tickets to offer more value per point through its travel portal. More airline relationships could help them offer more flights, more dates, or better redemption values. Qantas has already appeared in Points Boost, and American Airlines has participated without being a Chase transfer partner. But I’d love to see deeper relationships produce more opportunities to redeem at 2 cents per point for premium cabin tickets in the future. #6086. Barry Goldwater Saw a Way Out of the Wilderness

No matter how federal elections turn out, there’s always work to be done at the state and local levels.

Senator Barry Goldwater addresses supporters in Arizona during his 1964 presidential campaign.

Hulton-Deutsch Collection/Corbis via Getty Images

Barry Goldwater was acquainted with political setbacks. The morning after the 1964 presidential election, he could count the states he had won on two hands. Harder to number were the Americans who had spent that fall knocking on doors for the first time because a senator from Arizona had given voice to something they believed. Goldwater had asked them to help Americans reclaim power from Washington.

After the loss, Goldwater urged his supporters not to give up the fight for free markets, smaller government, and the American family. It was the collective conviction that Americans could build better lives for their families if they could keep more of what they earned and decide for themselves how to raise their children that kept these people invested in American politics.

Victor Riches is the President and CEO of the Goldwater Institute, leading the Institute’s efforts to help people in all 50 states live freer, happier lives.

#6085. Bipartisan process for picking GAO chief breaks down

Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., speaks during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee business meeting on Sept. 23. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.

Sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget. The White House submitted ethics paperwork on Ueland — required for nominations — to the GAO, according to a source.

Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., on Thursday posted notice of a committee hearing Nov. 19 to examine more than a dozen presidential nominees for executive and judicial offices, including “a nominee to be Comptroller General.”

The post identifies by name all of the nominees except the candidate for comptroller general. The post has been filled by an acting comptroller general, Orice Williams Brown, since Gene L. Dodaro completed his 15-year term at the end of last year.

The move by Paul to short-circuit the convening of a legislative commission to recommend candidates infuriated top Democrats, who excoriated the chairman in a joint statement Wednesday night. A special bipartisan, bicameral legislative commission is supposed to recommend at least three candidates for comptroller general to the president, according to statute.

Homeland Security Committee GOP staff solicited recommendations for a comptroller general from some Democratic congressional offices Wednesday afternoon, imposing a deadline of 8 a.m. Thursday, according to Democratic aides.

The president nominates the head of the GAO, the investigative arm of Congress, with the advice and consent of the Senate.

Paul pushed back on the criticism Thursday, saying, “Democrats have known about this for months and months and months.” He said the last time the special commission made recommendations for the office, when Barack Obama was president, “Democrats submitted their own list, Republicans submitted their own list. So they can complain all they want but they just need to make their list and submit it.”

In the past, however, the special commission convened, sought applications for the position, interviewed candidates and deliberated before sending recommendations to the president.

A 1980 law states that when there is a vacancy in the comptroller general position, “there is established a commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment to the vacant office,” and that the commission must submit at least three names.

Under the statute, the commission includes the speaker, Senate majority and minority leaders, House majority and minority leaders, chairs and ranking members of the Senate Homeland Security and House Oversight and Government Reform committees, and the Senate president pro tempore.

In 1981, for example, after the law took effect, the two congressional leaders, Speaker Thomas P. “Tip” O’Neill Jr., D-Mass., and Senate Majority Leader Howard H. Baker, R-Tenn., sent a letter to President Ronald Reagan saying the special commission had met and voted to recommend eight candidates to succeed Comptroller General Elmer Staats.

“The members of the Commission have taken their statutory responsibility seriously,” they wrote.

Reagan nominated Charles A. Bowsher, who was on the list, and he was confirmed.

After Bowsher’s term ended in 1996, the commission eventually formed, interviewed multiple candidates, and deliberated for several months. Republicans controlled both chambers, and Bill Clinton was president. The members of the commission could not reach agreement, and as a result, the Republicans on the committee submitted their list to Clinton, and the Democrats on the panel submitted theirs.

Clinton also had his own list. Clinton nominated David M. Walker, who was on all three lists, and he was confirmed by the Senate more than two years after Bowsher’s departure. Walker argued Thursday against short-circuiting the commission process.

“The position is of critical importance and the related statutory Commission process should not be circumvented," Walker said. "Doing so would undercut the credibility of the person and the effectiveness of the GAO.”

Walker resigned in March of 2008, when George W. Bush was still president. He appointed Dodaro as acting comptroller general when he left. The commission got going several months later, creating a website with application instructions and candidate questions.

Over the next two years, the commission interviewed some 20 candidates. Democrats and Republicans on the panel were unable to reach agreement, and Democrats, who had a majority on the commission, submitted their own list to Obama in 2010. Republicans followed up with their list.

“The Commission has been working in earnest on this undertaking for more than one year and has dedicated considerable time and effort to present you with highly qualified candidates for this important position,” then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., and then-Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, D-Nev., along with other Democratic leaders, wrote to Obama when they submitted the Democrats’ list.

The Democrats’ move drew a rebuke from Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, who was ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee at the time.

Collins said in a statement she was “extremely disappointed” that Democrats “abruptly ended the selection process for the next Comptroller General without a bipartisan agreement” on the recommendations. “We have had several exceptionally qualified individuals apply to be the next leader of the GAO, and it should have been possible to come up with a consensus list.”

Obama nominated and the Senate confirmed Dodaro, who was one of four recommendations from the Democrats.

#6084. World Of Hyatt Status Revamps For 2027—Award Stacking And New Benefit Choices, But Cuts Come Also

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

Hyatt will finally let members combine a free night certificate with a confirmed suite upgrade starting January 1, 2027. I’ve wanted that for years. They’re also extending milestone free night certificates from 180 days to a year, and adding rewards after just 10 qualifying nights.

This isn’t an across the board improvement. Suite upgrades will expire sooner. The suite upgrade choice at 50 nights gets cut in half. And My Hyatt Concierge becomes something you select alongside other rewards, rather than something everyone automatically receives at 60 nights. Free parking will no longer be an automatic benefit on award stays for Globalists.

When I covered Hyatt’s last major status benefit refresh in November 2023, I liked it overall. They made awards transferable, added choices, and let members try Globalist benefits before earning Globalist. Guest of Honor became limited, but the Milestone Rewards themselves mostly got better.

This time there are new and better options. I genuinely like a lot of the choices, but there are real tradeoffs. Hyatt is pitching the changes as more choice and flexibility, based on listening to members. That’s actually fair for much of this, though I don’t think members told them what they really wanted was for suite upgrade to expire up to a year earlier.

Hyatt will allow members to combine eligible awards on the same reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and the new Free Parking Awards. This fixes one of the problems I’ve been complaining about for years. A free night certificate is something you often want to use on a special leisure stay. That’s also when a suite may matter most, especially traveling with family. When I didn’t want to use a free night certificate was a work trip by myself. Free night awards had a lot less value to me because I had to give up a confirmed suite to use them. But being able to use the two awards together makes both more valuable. Combining Guest of Honor with a suite upgrade is useful, too. You can give someone Globalist treatment and confirm their suite ahead of time, rather than leaving the room upgrade to availability when they arrive. Hyatt also promises an enhanced Pay My Way experience, letting members mix awards, points, cash and Points + Cash by night. Online selection, gifting and redemption will be available for eligible awards. Pay My Way and stacking, by the way, really do all work together. Hyatt offers me this illustration, Let’s say a member is making a three night booking. Assuming both the Standard Suite was available for the duration, and there is award inventory available on the selected dates (just like today) – yes, a member could apply a Suite Upgrade Award to the whole stay, a Free Parking award to the whole stay, a Guest of Honor Award to the whole stay, and then pay for the reservation using points on one night, a promotional Free Night Award on another night, and cash on the third night.

Hyatt will allow members to combine eligible awards on the same reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and the new Free Parking Awards.

This fixes one of the problems I’ve been complaining about for years. A free night certificate is something you often want to use on a special leisure stay. That’s also when a suite may matter most, especially traveling with family. When I didn’t want to use a free night certificate was a work trip by myself. Free night awards had a lot less value to me because I had to give up a confirmed suite to use them. But being able to use the two awards together makes both more valuable.

Online selection, gifting and redemption will be available for eligible awards. Pay My Way and stacking, by the way, really do all work together. Hyatt offers me this illustration,

Let’s say a member is making a three night booking. Assuming both the Standard Suite was available for the duration, and there is award inventory available on the selected dates (just like today) – yes, a member could apply a Suite Upgrade Award to the whole stay, a Free Parking award to the whole stay, a Guest of Honor Award to the whole stay, and then pay for the reservation using points on one night, a promotional Free Night Award on another night, and cash on the third night.

Milestone Rewards currently begin at 20 qualifying nights. Next year they’ll start at 10 nights or 20,000 base points. Here’s the new chart through 50 nights. Qualifying nights / base points   What you receive 10 / 20,000   Choose one: 1 qualifying night credit, $25 FIND experience credit, or $30 Inclusive Collection spa credit. 20 / 35,000   Choose one: 2 qualifying night credits, $30 spa credit, $25 Delta certificate, 2K Next Stay Award, or 2 Club Access Awards. 30 / 50,000   Choose 10,000 bonus points or a Category 1–4 free night. Also choose one: 2 qualifying night credits, $30 spa credit, $25 Delta certificate, 2K Next Stay Award, or 2 Club Access Awards. 40 / 65,000   Receive 1 Guest of Honor Award. Also choose one: 5 qualifying night credits, $200 Thompson Hotels credit, $75 Delta certificate, 5,000 points, or 1 Suite Upgrade Award. 50 / 80,000   Choose one: $200 Thompson Hotels credit, $75 Delta certificate, 5,000 points, or 1 Suite Upgrade Award. The qualifying night choices add up to 10 nights: one at the first milestone, two at the next, two at 30 nights and five at 40 nights. These count toward both status and Milestone Rewards. That creates a path to Globalist with 50 qualifying nights from other sources, if you select all four night rewards. The requirement remains 60, but 10 can come from these choices. And you earn qualifying nights with the The World Of Hyatt Credit Card (See rates and fees) too – 5 qualifying night credits every year and 2 qualifying night every time you spend $5,000 on the card. The 30 night option to take 10,000 points instead of a Category 1–4 certificate is useful for someone who struggles to use the certificate. A good Category 4 redemption can be worth more, and the certificate will become easier to use with the longer expiration and ability to add a suite upgrade. One Fewer Suite Upgrade, And A Choice About Your Concierge The reduction at 50 nights is easy to miss. The current choice is two Suite Upgrade Awards. The new chart offers one. At 60 nights or 100,000 base points, members will receive: 2 Guest of Honor Awards. A choice of free nights: 2 Category 1–4 awards or 1 Category 1–7 award. Two selections from this menu: 7,500 bonus points, a Free Parking Award, a $100 Delta certificate, 2 Suite Upgrade Awards, or My Hyatt Concierge. You can still select the two suite upgrades and concierge access, keeping the existing 60 night package. But if you want points or parking, something else has to go. And you can’t make the same two choices at 60 nights – you can’t have four upgrades, 15,000 points or two parking awards. You don’t have o select all of your awards at once, though you do have to make these two selections at the same time. Hyatt explains to me that you’ll still have 90 days to make your choices, and: In milestones where there are separate choices, such as 30 nights, the member can make those choices at different points within the 90 day selection window (e.g., could choose the Free Night Award one day, and the HIC Spa credit on a different day.) At 60 nights, the member can choose their free night award choice on a different day from the other selection, but the two selections within “Choose Two” must be made together at the same time. I do plan to keep the concierge benefit, even though mine has never been very responsive. I won’t give up the ability to email someone to address issues. I just wish I would hear back more quickly, and didn’t need to follow up so often. Maybe that’s actually coming? Hyatt tells me they do plan greater investment in the concierge program: [B]y shifting to a choice, we will be able to further invest in My Hyatt Concierge and deliver even more proactive and personalized care. We will share more when available.

Milestone Rewards currently begin at 20 qualifying nights. Next year they’ll start at 10 nights or 20,000 base points. Here’s the new chart through 50 nights.

The qualifying night choices add up to 10 nights: one at the first milestone, two at the next, two at 30 nights and five at 40 nights. These count toward both status and Milestone Rewards.

That creates a path to Globalist with 50 qualifying nights from other sources, if you select all four night rewards. The requirement remains 60, but 10 can come from these choices. And you earn qualifying nights with the The World Of Hyatt Credit Card (See rates and fees) too – 5 qualifying night credits every year and 2 qualifying night every time you spend $5,000 on the card.

The 30 night option to take 10,000 points instead of a Category 1–4 certificate is useful for someone who struggles to use the certificate. A good Category 4 redemption can be worth more, and the certificate will become easier to use with the longer expiration and ability to add a suite upgrade.

You can still select the two suite upgrades and concierge access, keeping the existing 60 night package. But if you want points or parking, something else has to go.

And you can’t make the same two choices at 60 nights – you can’t have four upgrades, 15,000 points or two parking awards. You don’t have o select all of your awards at once, though you do have to make these two selections at the same time. Hyatt explains to me that you’ll still have 90 days to make your choices, and:

In milestones where there are separate choices, such as 30 nights, the member can make those choices at different points within the 90 day selection window (e.g., could choose the Free Night Award one day, and the HIC Spa credit on a different day.) At 60 nights, the member can choose their free night award choice on a different day from the other selection, but the two selections within “Choose Two” must be made together at the same time.

I do plan to keep the concierge benefit, even though mine has never been very responsive. I won’t give up the ability to email someone to address issues. I just wish I would hear back more quickly, and didn’t need to follow up so often. Maybe that’s actually coming? Hyatt tells me they do plan greater investment in the concierge program:

[B]y shifting to a choice, we will be able to further invest in My Hyatt Concierge and deliver even more proactive and personalized care. We will share more when available.

As before, lifetime Globalists retain their concierge without having to stay 60 nights.

The new parking award covers a qualifying paid or award stay of up to seven nights, and can be gifted. It appears among the choices at 60, 70, 80 and 90 nights. However it’s no longer simply a benefit for Globalists redeeming points for free nights. I wrote in that Hyatt was surveying turning automatic benefits into awards you could choose and they’ve done that with this one. The benefit is no longer unlimited It comes with a tradeoff – the benefit is instead of something else And you have to plan ahead, one more thing to track and manage, rather than something that’s just ‘taken care of’ in recognition of your loyalty. Hyatt explains the decision to me as, [T]his decision was made as 70% of Globalists did not use the free parking benefit in 2025; 95% used it 4 times or less, and moving this to a choice allowed the program to retain it for members who value it and introduce other exciting new awards like the $200 Thompson Hotels Credit and the $500 Premium Suite Credit. If the benefit wasn’t being used, it actually wasn’t that expensive to offer! And not using it regularly doesn’t mean the option isn’t valued. It may not have been the most valuable benefit of Globalist for most people, but I wouldn’t personally make the tradeoff (in fairness, I’m someone that did use and get value from it). Of course, a parking award will be eligible for use a paid stay while it previously was only available on points. However, at 70, 80 or 90 nights where you can claim it you’re passing up 10,000 points or a suite upgrade to select it. A Year To Use Every Award Is Both An Improvement And A Cut Hyatt’s release presents the new expiration policy as giving members extra time. That’s true for some awards, but the effect runs in both directions. Hyatt tells me, For all awards issued on January 1, 2027 or later, expiration dates will be 365 days from the date of issuance. Milestone free night awards that currently expire after 180 days will get substantially more time. But suite upgrades, ordinary Milestone Guest of Honor awards and club access awards currently have much longer lives, generally through the end of the year earned plus another 14 months under Hyatt’s existing rules. A suite upgrade selected January 1, 2026 remained valid through February 2028. Under a 365 day rule, the same issuance date would produce a January 1, 2027 expiration. That’s more than a year of usefulness gone. Shortening the window makes it harder to hold upgrades for a major trip, to book far ahead, or to save awards from a heavy travel year for a quieter one. Note that this change applies to Milestone Rewards earned starting in 2027. So any that you earn at the end of 2026, and redeem in 2027, follow the old rules. Hyatt confirms, Only awards earned and selected after January 1, 2027 follow the new 365 expiration from issuance. So, a 2026 award (even if selected in 2027) would carry the current 2026 expiration rules. More Free Night Choices And Delta Status At Higher Milestones Here’s the rest of the 2027 chart: Qualifying nights   What you receive 70, 80 and 90, at each milestone   1 Guest of Honor Award, plus choose one: a Free Parking Award, 2 single visit Delta Sky Club passes, 10,000 points, or 1 Suite Upgrade Award. 100   Choose 1 Category 1–7 night, 2 Category 1–4 nights, or a $500 premium suite credit. Also choose one: Delta Gold Medallion, 10,000 points, 1 Suite Upgrade Award, or a Miraval Extra Night Award. 110, 120, 130 and 140, at each milestone   1 Guest of Honor Award, plus choose one: Delta Gold Medallion, 10,000 points, 1 Suite Upgrade Award, or a Miraval Extra Night Award. 150   Choose 2 Category 1–7 nights or an Ultimate Free Night Award. Also choose one: Delta Platinum Medallion, 10,000 points, 1 Suite Upgrade Award, or a Miraval Extra Night Award. The Ultimate Free Night at 150 nights isn’t going away. The two Category 1–7 nights are an alternative. Someone who wants two nights at less expensive hotels can choose those, while someone planning one especially expensive night can retain the Ultimate award, which covers participating Category 1–8 hotels, Category A–F all-inclusives and Miraval. The new hotel credits are more restrictive than points: $30 Inclusive Collection spa credit: for spa treatments at participating all-inclusive resorts. $200 Thompson Hotels credit: toward an eligible paid stay. $500 premium suite credit: toward an eligible paid premium suite stay of at least two nights. I’ve wanted a way to use two suite upgrades to confirm a premium suite. A discount on buying a premium suite isn’t as attractive to me. But there are times I might use it. Delta Gold starting at 100 nights and Platinum at 150 nights are interesting choices for someone who flies Delta without status. I still preferred the American partnership. The ability to redeem Hyatt points for American status for a trip was useful for people who didn’t have American status. And the earlier version earned American miles on Hyatt stays. I’d rather earn those than Delta miles. FIND credits are being pared back sharply. The $25 choices at 20 and 30 nights disappear, as do $150 choices at 40 and 50 nights and $300 choices at 70, 80 and 90. A $25 FIND choice appears at the new 10 night milestone. What Hyatt Gets From These Changes The strongest improvements are award stacking, more time to use free night certificates, an earlier first reward, and choices that let members avoid awards they won’t use. A member who doesn’t value concierge access can get something else, while someone who prefers two less expensive hotel nights can choose them. I expect members approaching Globalist will like the qualifying night choices. People who lose free night certificates to expiration should come out ahead, too. Existing Globalists who use all their suite upgrades, plan trips far ahead, or regularly choose FIND experiences have more to lose. Hyatt also gets more ways to influence where members spend. A Thompson credit encourages a paid Thompson stay. A spa credit encourages a treatment that may cost much more than the credit. The premium suite credit encourages someone to buy a room they might otherwise try to upgrade into. Shorter suite award validity should leave fewer outstanding upgrades available for future use. Making concierge elective lets members reveal whether they value the service more than points or another reward. And offering status credits makes the next milestone feel closer, encouraging someone with a modest number of Hyatt nights to keep going. For me, being able to confirm a suite on a free night certificate is the biggest improvement. I care much more about that than a spa coupon. There really is more choice and the ability to earn status faster with these changes. Stacking and combining rewards is great. So is longer expiration of free night awards, though sadly at the cost of shorter expiration for suite upgrade awards. The most consequential change for me might be something that isn’t really being announced. If changing My Hyatt Concierge to a choice benefit really does entail greater investment in the program, it would make the experience far more premium and secure even greater loyalty. The strongest improvements are award stacking, more time to use free night certificates, an earlier first reward, and choices that let members avoid awards they won’t use. A member who doesn’t value concierge access can get something else, while someone who prefers two less expensive hotel nights can choose them.

I expect members approaching Globalist will like the qualifying night choices. People who lose free night certificates to expiration should come out ahead, too. Existing Globalists who use all their suite upgrades, plan trips far ahead, or regularly choose FIND experiences have more to lose.

Hyatt also gets more ways to influence where members spend. A Thompson credit encourages a paid Thompson stay. A spa credit encourages a treatment that may cost much more than the credit. The premium suite credit encourages someone to buy a room they might otherwise try to upgrade into.

Shorter suite award validity should leave fewer outstanding upgrades available for future use. Making concierge elective lets members reveal whether they value the service more than points or another reward. And offering status credits makes the next milestone feel closer, encouraging someone with a modest number of Hyatt nights to keep going.

For me, being able to confirm a suite on a free night certificate is the biggest improvement. I care much more about that than a spa coupon.

There really is more choice and the ability to earn status faster with these changes. Stacking and combining rewards is great. So is longer expiration of free night awards, though sadly at the cost of shorter expiration for suite upgrade awards.

The most consequential change for me might be something that isn’t really being announced. If changing My Hyatt Concierge to a choice benefit really does entail greater investment in the program, it would make the experience far more premium and secure even greater loyalty.

Gary Leff is one of the foremost experts in the field of miles, points, and frequent business travel - a topic he has covered since 2002. Co-founder of frequent flyer community InsideFlyer.com, emcee of the Freddie Awards, and named one of the "World's Top Travel Experts" by Conde' Nast Traveler (2010-Present) Gary has been a guest on most major news media, profiled in several top print publications, and published broadly on the topic of consumer loyalty. Hyatt’s concierge service for globalists is generally useless.

So while having to choose concierge service over other benefits is a devaluation of globalist service, it’s, practically speaking, not a huge loss for most members.

The loss of free parking on award-redemption stays is somewhat similar. On paper, it’s a significant devaluation. However, how many guests actually use it? If I’m going a resort, I’m not arriving with a car. Same for if I’m redeeming points to stay at the Park Hyatt in Paris or wherever. So, practically speaking, it may not be a huge loss for many elites.

What I don’t understand is why wouldn’t you come up with better offerings for globalists who do 100, 120 or 150+ nights?

I wish they would have created a benefit to compensate for the growing number of Hyatt Regency and Grand Hyatt properties WITHOUT an open or operational club lounge.

By the way, I would note that eliminating free parking on award stays is great for owners/franchisees. They can’t charge you a resort or destination fee. But now they can charge you $70 or $100 for parking that used to be free. In short, it’s a way to extract a portion of the revenue lost from waived resort or destination fees from a segment of guests who arrive with a car and want to park it at the hotel.

Outstanding article, Gary, with a lot of nuance missed by others. Don’t know if your Hyatt contacts gave you the answer to this, but if you don’t choose a Concierge at 60 nights, will you still have access to the Globalist telephone number? I have used my Concierge once or twice in the last five years, but I have used the Globalist line quite a bit.

Hi Gary. Do you know if not selecting the concierge benefit next year will still give you access to the concierge line? I can live without the MHC, but the concierge line is something I frequently use for everything.

Soooooo what if a Globalist gives another member a Guest of Honor award? Presumably the GofH will no longer be eligible to receive free parking?

@PH – GoH on its own will no longer mean free parking on award redemption, you’d have to gift both a goh + free parking award if you want them to have both but they’ll stack

Interesting. I have used the free parking benefit four times a year in New York. Andaz charges $90/nt for my suv. That’s nearly $200 for two nts The other times have been at other properties for $45-$65/nt for 6 nts@ around $300. I would say that’s a significant devaluation.

@DSK – having a concierge doesn’t preclude you from using the globalist number, but you can also just use the concierge # to speak with a concierge even if your own is not available

I think for the most part, (other than the switch from AA to DL) these are positive improvements overall. When is the last time you could say that about ANY loyalty program? Almost everything I’ve written to Hyatt about for the past two years has finally occurred…particularly the 1 yr expiration on threshold night awards. I agree with @FNT Delta Diamond that they need to enhance the rewards for power users…Perhaps for 2028 they could institute a “rollover” option for elites with 110+ nights: maybe allow excess nights above 100 to rollover to the next year’s qualifying year so that Globalist renewal is automatic or much easier? Or perhaps a single year “boost” if one doesn’t hit 60 in the next year? Just a thought. As this shows, it never hurts to ask!

Rooms for points mostly grossly overpriced. Chase transfer cut last straw. No bueno

I call BS on Hyatt saying Globalists don’t use the free parking. This actively costs them hard cash and they wanted to minimize the cash outlay.

Of course Globalists are using free parking on award stays. They are going after the travel hacking community and not the road warriors who earn Globalist on paid stays, because they weren’t getting free parking on paid stays. Easy for them to blur those lines but we can see through their statement.

https://youtube.com/shorts/WpGW1-wVv7Y?si=uSj-ikgis-9UnX4b

I feel it’s overall a downgrade, but like the fact that FNA will last longer, and the ability to stack awards is great. Also, if the online booking upgrades work the way intended, I don’t know that I will need a concierge. That’s the main thing I call for (combine an award and cash booking, and use on SNA, for example).

I see this as almost entirely a devaluation. Most of the new choices strike me as borderline thoughtless/pointless additions – the award at ten nights is basically useless for me and I’m honestly tempted to ignore it when it hits (probably by mid-January) – and whatever their bloviation may say, when the parking thing matters, it makes a big effing dent, and parking fees are showing up in more and more dubiously-justified places all the time. Losing that would be worth throwing the baby out with the bath water here, and possibly throwing the bath out as well – the “alternatives” it let them introduce aren’t worth the trade.

I realize that perspectives can legitimately vary, but this is a noticeable devaluation with a few minimal bright spots (being better able to bundle three Cat 1-7 awards is nice), but taken as a whole I’d rather tell them to shove the whole package somewhere the sun don’t shine.

To the extent they claim to have been trying to improve the program, they failed miserably and should feel bad about their efforts.

Overall a devaluation, but not a large one. Neither of the key improvements I’ve repeatedly suggested happened (make club awards useable for breakfast at hotels without a club, make cat 1-4 night awards cat 1-5 or 1-6 so they covered most “normal” hotels as they used to).

losing globalist free parking on award stays is a sizable loss. for 2026 qualified globalists, hyatt should add 1-4 free parking awards in 2027 to soften thid unexpected blow. cc spending globalists will feel the brunt. many will rethink and some change 2027 cc spending habits.

I’ve got a reservation using points for NYE + 2 nights. So, am I going to get screwed on the free parking? Of course, this is the first time having to park a car on a points stay in a long time.

They badly need the option to top up cat 1-4 certs with points like Marriott has. The desirable properties keep getting moved to cat 5.

I have a problem with taking away free parking. Do we know if the new rules are taking effect January 1, 2027 for those earning Globalist for 2027? We would not have had the option to get a free parking pass as yet.

Hi Gary, Great review! Any change to the number and type of awards given to lifetime globalist?

Once again, the shorter expiration date on the suite upgrade awards may cause some to delay achieving a milestone so they could have one to use in December, January, or February. Hopefully they still keep the 90 day period to choose.

I like the changes and excellent analysis, Gary-very fair reading!

Now, I want to know when the premium Hyatt card will be launched and what mechanisms it will have to shorten one’s way towards Globalist.

Along those lines, will Hyatt permit holders of this card to top off any and or all certificates? Marriott has permittied this, IHG has permitted this and it is time that Hyatt does as well, seeing that Chase issues cards for all 3 chains.

Moreover, it will be in the spirit of permitting a milestone award seeker a more tailored award.

I may not value many Category 7 properties, but perhaps a Category 5 or 6 speaks more to me — if given a choice between 2 Category 4 awards that can be topped off as opposed to 1 Category 7 award, the choice would be easy.

Gary, I have until Jan 21 to make my choice for 50 nights. I used to wait until January to get the longer expiration date (Feb 2029 instead of Feb 2028).

Does this impact choices already earned in other words if I wait until January to choose I will get a shorter expiration date that if I for the suite upgrade awards then if I chose in December?

Anyone know if you earn a milestone in 2026 but select it in 2027 if it will have a Feb 2029 expiration? You have 90 days to choose I can’t imagine two different expiration dates based on when issued but maybe?

My reaction: Cat 1-4 awards remain close to useless. Fix that and we can talk.

Loss of parking sucks. We drive to the Hyatt Regency Huntington Beach resort and parking is $60 a night. Kids grew up at the resort. My concierge has been super helpful. Booking the suite at Grand Hyatt Tokyo you can’t select 4 people to book a standard room but a suite can sleep 4 so I had to call into the concierge to explain the issue since I couldn’t book online and she was able to book us with points apply the SUA and change to 4 person occupancy. Maybe I can do that without a concierge but it sure helps to have someone on the phone doing that for me. Love the upgrade on free night certificates.

@nsx at FlyerTalk — For. Real. Dawg. For. Real.

@principal lewis – LALF stated that Globalist status earned in 2026 included free parking until Feb 2028 so, based on that, they plan to honor it next year. IMHO, a borderline change. Sure I used it a few times if I traveled and rented a car but much of my travel is international w no car. Also, someone complained about it being removed for road warriors who stayed 60 plus nights – well I suspect you are traveling on OPM and can expense the parking so, again, no big loss.

The loss of parking will directly impact me. I think I’ve probably used that on 6 nights this year, including valet at PH Auckland and Seabird. And while I never email my concierge, I do frequently call the concierge number and greatly value the fast, competent service.

The 365 day expiration for a SUA is horrible. No longer possible to confirm a SUA before registration opens. And if trying to secure a suite a year in advance, you have to time when you earn the reward. This is an incentive to stay elsewhere so you don’t hit the milestone too early and have to select an award before you want it.

Also, can premium suite discount be used on a cash + points booking?

#6083. Demand For $1,589 In Rental Car Damage Dropped After Pointing Out Illegal Fees

Sixt demanded $1,589 from a customer for splatter and scuffs on a rental car, including nearly $500 in illegal fees. The customer disputed the claim, complained to consumer agencies, and says it went to collections anyway. The bill disappeared once the practice came under scrutiny. Christopher Nienhuis, a Colorado resident, rented a Buick at Milwaukee airport in October while visiting Marquette University. Days after returning it, he received a damage bill for black splatter around the license plate and near the tires, along with white scuffing around the rear windshield. He says he didn’t cause the damage and that the black material could simply be washed off. Sixt dropped the claim a week after being contacted by a news reporter. Four Renters Were Billed Fees Wisconsin Doesn’t Allow Four customers with disputed claims from the same airport location complained of illegal charges. Todd Lofgren: $6,265 for “graffiti.” He described white specks near a tire and along the bumper. The photos and invoice were dated August 18, three days after he returned the car. The bill included $1,161 in prohibited fees. Sixt dropped it September 28 after he challenged it through multiple channels. Brenda Bassett: nearly $600 for a dent already documented. The rear dent was listed in her rental agreement before she took the 2025 Toyota. About $137 consisted of diminished value and appraisal fees. A September 15 letter came from Strala Group, which handles claims for Sixt. The claim was dropped. Autumn Wojciechowski: $872 for a scratch underneath the car. She’d photographed the vehicle before driving away, but not its underside. Nearly $200 of her October 2025 damage invoice consisted of prohibited fees. This claim was dropped, too. All four claims have been withdrawn. Wisconsin law limits damage liability to reasonable repair costs, reflecting discounts available to the rental company, or the vehicle’s value before the damage, whichever is lower. Loss of use, administrative charges and appraisal fees are prohibited. Diminished value charges (loss in resale value) aren’t allowed either. Sixt Already Settled A Damage Billing Lawsuit Sixt’s 2025 damage billing settlement addressed allegations involving estimated repairs, diminished value, loss of use and administrative charges. The $11 million package included about $2.87 million in potential refunds and $6.6 million in abandoned collection claims, along with legal and administrative costs. The incentives are lousy. A customer can pay to make a collection demand go away, turn it over to insurance, or spend hours fighting. If the company withdraws a bad claim only when someone gets enough attention, everyone else still has to decide whether contesting it is worth the trouble. I’ve called rental car fees the scammiest in travel. These damage add-ons are especially difficult to comparison shop because you don’t discover them until after you’ve returned the car. Sixt Isn’t Great, But You Expect Charges To Be Correct I’ve found Sixt offers an inferior experience in the U.S. market. My Miami rental years ago involved a Mercedes they didn’t and a proposed alternative of a $30 a day upgrade for a lesser car. I canceled and went to National. The Milwaukee airport said its lease requires Sixt to follow the law and allows termination for an uncured violation after notice. But the airport said it was waiting for the state consumer protection agency to determine that a violation occurred. It’s not yet clear whether they’ve stopped charging these fees in Wisconsin. Topics on this pageCar rentalConsumer protectionSixtWisconsinColoradoMercedes-BenzMiamiMilwaukeeToyota+5 more More From View from the Wing

This is common practice in Europe. Hertz sent me an invoice and charged my credit card almost a year after a rental in Germany for $460.00 for “damages.” I disputed the charges as I still had my return showing that they signed off with no damage. AMEX refunded my money, so Hertz turned it over to a collection agency in PA. They called me and I told them to go to hell and sue me. The collection dude said, “No one is going to sue you for $460.00,” so I sent them a letter telling them to cease and desist contacting me about the charge and if they wanted to sue, I was willing to counter sue as I had paperwork saying the car was returned undamaged. Last I heard of it and it never turned up on my credit report. Every time I rent in Europe, I get dinged for a toll, or in Italy it was for driving in a “congested area.” You figure they steal $100 to $200 from every renter, that is a good chunk of change a year.

Sixt got me for some damage that I know I didn’t cause. I didn’t think I needed to record video of the car after I brought it back. Credit card CDW paid for 90% of it except for a lost depreciation fee of $200. Snakey.

Im not going to no collections over a damage dispute. Ruining my credit? Pay for it and sue later.

I don’t rent cars very often, but when I do, I video the entire exterior and interior at pickup and again when I return the car along with the guy/girl I hand the keys to. I had one of these BS damage incidents several years ago and I got dinged for something I didn’t do and it was a couple months after I rented. Fortunately I was still in possession of the turn in receipt so I didn’t have to pay. All that being said, they are scam artists of the 10th degree and I don’t trust any of them.. Video and photograph your rentals.

Avis is notorious for ‘cleaning fees’. 9 times out of 10 the claim is dropped. It is important to take pics before AND after.

Maybe I’ve just been lucky, but this is (one of the reasons) why I like National. They don’t seem to want to nickel and dime you over everything. The “allowed” amount of damage is pretty generous. I’ve never had them hassle me over anything. And the refill costs if you bring a car back not full of fuel aren’t totally ridiculous either.

Wisconsin law also requires rental car companies to provide you with independent damage appraisals and a right to inspect before they can just charge you for damages. I once got billed by Avis for repairs for damage that I didn’t cause weeks after my rental. I challenged it to the Avis General Counsel’s office, pointing out that they didn’t follow the law, and they dropped the charges.

It really amazes me Congress doesn’t take on Hertz and now Sixt. This is literally a 99.9% issue. You would get so much publicity and public support.

I had one management job where I had a lot of my team traveli to UK. There was a span where my company was between.major rental contracts in Europe, and in the interim they were pointing us to Sixt, and unlike in the US, we self-insured. SIxt was really good at finding (plastic) wheel cover scuffs and paint scratches, consistently $700 to 800 GBP. Fortunately, they were not selected for the new contract. My company has about 4000 people on travel at any given time.

#6082. 14 tricks to getting the most value from your cruise vacations

Learn how to get started earning and redeeming rewards so you can make the most of your everyday spending.

See how far your points, miles and dollars go in TPG's first loyalty report.

See how TPG ranks the top US airlines for 2026.

Melinda Crow is a Texas-based freelance writer and guidebook author. From camping to cruising, she's been writing about travel for 30-plus years. Her first cruise was on Carnival’s second ship, Carnivale. She prefers shore excursions involving history, wine or wildlife.

Editorial note: This is a recurring post, regularly updated with new information and offers.
